paper.title: Optimal Resource Allocation with Semi-Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Linear stochastic resource allocation with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: Action: continuous allocation M_{k,t} >= 0 with sum_k M_{k,t} <= 1 (resources replenished each round)
Job k succeeds w.p. min{1, M_{k,t}/nu_k} with unknown cut-off nu_k in (0, inf]; reward is number of completed jobs
The learner knows lower bounds 0 < underline{nu}_{k,0} <= nu_k for each job (removable via the halving initialisation of Section 6)
Jobs assumed to have distinct parameters nu_1 < nu_2 < ... < nu_K
settings.definition_quote: In each time-step $t$ the learner chooses $M_{k,t} \geq 0$ subject to the constraint, $\sum_{k=1}^K M_{k,t} \leq 1$. Then all jobs are executed and $X_{k,t} \in \set{0,1}$ indicates the success or failure of job $k$ in time-step $t$ and is sampled from a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $\beta(M_{k,t} / \nu_k) \defined \min\set{1, M_{k,t} / \nu_k}$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected success probabilities (pseudo-regret). Since c_k1 ~ log(T), the bound is O(ell log^2 T + ... + sum log T/Delta_{ell+1,k}); the paper states this O-form in eq. (big-o-theorem) assuming eta_k = O(1), which Proposition 11 (E eta <= 4 with halving initialisation) justifies. The u_{k,j} in the statement is a typo for u_{j,k}. Running time O(1) per job per step.

source.quote: Given fixed $n$ and $8n \geq K \geq 2$ and an arbitrary algorithm, there exists an allocation problem for which the expected regret satisfies $R_n \geq {\sqrt{nK} \over 16 \sqrt{2}}$.

results.notes: Hard instances: nu_j = 2 for j != k, nu_k = 2/(1+eps), eps = sqrt(K/(8n)).
